content: Do not stop taking dolutegravir or any other HIV medications, even for a short period, unless explicitly instructed by your doctor. Common side effects of dolutegravir include headaches and difficulty sleeping. These effects are generally mild, but if they persist or worsen, consult your healthcare provider. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to your health outweigh the potential risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to combat infections that were previously present in your body, potentially causing symptoms of those diseases to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune response may occur, leading to symptoms. This reaction can happen at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or even months later. Severe allergic reactions to dolutegravir are rare. However, if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing, seek immediate medical attention. This is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before starting dolutegravir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. If you are pregnant, inform your doctor before using this medication. Dolutegravir can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. However, this medication does pass into breast milk, so discuss breastfeeding with your doctor. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking dolutegravir, regular laboratory and medical tests (such as liver and kidney function, viral load, and T-cell counts) should be performed to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store dolutegravir at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. For 10-milligram tablets, keep them in their original container with the desiccant (drying agent) inside. Ensure the bottle is tightly closed when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for disposal instructions. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. Dolutegravir, commonly sold under the brand name Tivicay, is used in combination with other HIV medications to control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. This decreases the risk of HIV-related complications, such as new infections or cancer, and improves your quality of life. Dolutegravir belongs to a class of drugs known as integrase inhibitors. It is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods (such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams) during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Do not share personal items (such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors) that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. Read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting dolutegravir and each time you get a refill. Take this medication at least two hours before or six hours after taking sucralfate or products containing aluminum or magnesium (such as antacids, laxatives, or buffered medications). If you are also taking calcium or iron supplements (including vitamins/minerals containing calcium or iron), take dolutegravir at least two hours before or six hours after these products. The dosage of dolutegravir is based on your medical condition, response to treatment, age, and other medications you may be taking. For children, the dosage is also determined by weight. It is crucial to continue taking this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Do not take more or less of this drug than prescribed, and do not stop taking it (or other HIV medications) even for a short time unless directed by your doctor.
